units.title: Safety Standards and Procedures in Network Cabling

learning_outcomes.description: Understand the importance of safety standards in network cabling

performance_criteria.description: Explain relevant safety standards and regulations in the network cabling industry (e.g., OSHA, ISO, NEC).
Explain the importance of following safety standards to prevent accidents, electrical hazards, and ensure personal and team safety.
Describe the consequences of non-compliance with safety standards in network installation projects.

learning_outcomes.description: Recognize potential hazards in the network installation environment

performance_criteria.description: Identify common hazards in network cabling environments, such as electrical risks, tripping hazards, and sharp tools.
Assess risks in a work area before beginning cabling tasks to ensure safety.
Recommend appropriate mitigation strategies to reduce hazards during cabling and installation.

learning_outcomes.description: Use appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for network cabling tasks

performance_criteria.description: Identify the correct PPE required for network cabling tasks (e.g., safety gloves, safety glasses, hard hats).
Demonstrate the correct use of PPE to ensure personal safety during installation and maintenance.
Inspect PPE before use to ensure it is in good condition and meets safety requirements.

learning_outcomes.description: Follow safe work practices during network cabling installation

performance_criteria.description: Apply lockout/tagout procedures to electrical systems to prevent electrical shock during cabling tasks.
Safely handle tools, such as cable cutters, strippers, and crimpers, following safety procedures.
Maintain a clean and organized work area to reduce the risk of accidents and ensure safe movement around the installation site.

learning_outcomes.description: Safely dispose of materials and equipment

performance_criteria.description: Identify the proper disposal methods for materials used in network cabling (e.g., cables, insulation, packaging).
Safely store and dispose of hazardous materials, such as batteries or chemicals, following environmental safety regulations.
Demonstrate the ability to clean up after installation tasks while adhering to environmental safety standards.

units.title: Teamwork and Collaboration in Network Installations

learning_outcomes.description: Understand the role of teamwork in network installation projects

performance_criteria.description: Explain the importance of teamwork in completing network installation tasks efficiently and on time.
Identify individual roles and responsibilities within a team during a network installation project.
Describe how effective teamwork contributes to safety and quality in network installation processes.

learning_outcomes.description: Collaborate effectively with team members on network cabling tasks

performance_criteria.description: Communicate task objectives and responsibilities clearly with team members to ensure mutual understanding.
Demonstrate the ability to assist other team members in completing tasks to maintain project flow.
Resolve conflicts or disagreements with team members constructively, without disrupting project progress.

learning_outcomes.description: Follow supervisory guidance and instructions during network installations

performance_criteria.description: Interpret instructions from supervisors or team leads accurately to ensure compliance with project requirements.
Demonstrate the ability to ask for clarification when instructions or tasks are not fully understood.
Execute tasks according to the supervisory plan, adjusting to changes in instruction as needed.

learning_outcomes.description: Manage tasks and time effectively within a team environment

performance_criteria.description: Prioritize tasks based on project timelines and team objectives.
Monitor task progress and adjust work pace to ensure deadlines are met without compromising quality.
Coordinate with team members to ensure seamless task handovers and continuity of work.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate a positive attitude and work ethic in a team setting

performance_criteria.description: Show respect for diverse team members by valuing their input and contributions.
Maintain a positive attitude, even in challenging situations, to foster a supportive team environment.
Uphold professional standards by being punctual, reliable, and committed to delivering high-quality work.

units.title: Communication Skills for Network Installation Projects

learning_outcomes.description: Understand the importance of communication in network cabling projects

performance_criteria.description: Explain why clear and effective communication is essential in coordinating tasks within network cabling projects.
Identify potential consequences of poor communication in network installation and maintenance activities.
Recognize the role of communication in ensuring safety, efficiency, and adherence to project specifications.

learning_outcomes.description: Communicate effectively with supervisors and team members

performance_criteria.description: Demonstrate the ability to listen actively and follow verbal and written instructions from supervisors.
Use appropriate technical terminology when discussing project tasks with team members and supervisors.
Provide clear and concise updates on task progress, challenges, or delays to supervisors in a timely manner.

learning_outcomes.description: Write clear and accurate reports and documentation

performance_criteria.description: Draft task reports that accurately reflect the status of network cabling work, including completed tasks and any issues encountered.
Ensure documentation is organized, legible, and free from errors, following standard formats for technical reporting.
Submit reports and documentation on time, as required by the project or supervisor.

learning_outcomes.description: Engage in professional communication with clients or stakeholders

performance_criteria.description: Demonstrate polite and professional communication when interacting with clients or stakeholders on-site.
Explain technical information or project status to clients in clear, non-technical language.
Handle client inquiries or concerns with a positive attitude, escalating issues to supervisors when necessary.

learning_outcomes.description: Use digital communication tools effectively in network cabling projects

performance_criteria.description: Demonstrate proficiency in using email, messaging apps, and other digital tools to communicate project updates or instructions.
Ensure messages sent through digital tools are clear, concise, and professional.
Follow proper protocols for documenting and storing digital communication related to network cabling projects.

units.title: Introduction to Network Cabling and Infrastructure

learning_outcomes.description: Understand the fundamentals of network cabling systems

performance_criteria.description: Describe the different types of network cables, including twisted pair (e.g., Cat5e, Cat6), coaxial, and fiber optic cables.
Explain the basic principles of how network cables transmit data, including signal types and data rates.
Identify the components of a network cabling system, such as cables, connectors, patch panels, and network devices.
Compare the advantages and limitations of different types of cables for various networking scenarios.
Explain the role of cabling standards (e.g., TIA/EIA) in ensuring compatibility and performance.

learning_outcomes.description: Recognize and describe different network topologies

performance_criteria.description: Define with illustrations, common network topologies, including star, bus, ring, and mesh.
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of each network topology in terms of scalability, reliability, and maintenance.
Identify the impact of network topology on cabling requirements and network performance.
Describe how topology influences network design decisions and the implementation of cabling infrastructure.

learning_outcomes.description: Understand basic network design principles

performance_criteria.description: Explain the concept of structured cabling and its importance in network design.
Describe the role of network design documents, such as floor plans and cable diagrams, in planning and implementing cabling projects.
Identify the factors that affect cable placement and routing, such as electrical interference, physical barriers, and distance limitations.
Discuss best practices for ensuring future scalability and flexibility in network design.

learning_outcomes.description: Identify and use common network cabling tools and equipment

performance_criteria.description: List and describe the functions of tools commonly used in network cabling, such as cable testers, crimpers, and punch-down tools.
Demonstrate the correct usage of these tools for tasks like cable preparation, termination, and testing.
Explain how to maintain and calibrate network cabling tools to ensure accurate performance.
Identify safety precautions associated with using network cabling tools and equipment.

learning_outcomes.description: Introduction to network cable installation and maintenance

performance_criteria.description: Describe the basic steps involved in installing network cables, including measuring, cutting, and terminating cables.
Explain routine maintenance tasks for network cabling, such as checking for wear and tear, and verifying cable performance.
Identify common issues in cable installation and maintenance and discuss methods for troubleshooting these issues.
Demonstrate proper cable management techniques to ensure organized and efficient cabling systems.

learning_outcomes.description: Understand and apply cable routing and laying techniques

performance_criteria.description: Describe the principles of cable routing, including methods for minimizing signal interference and maintaining signal integrity.
Demonstrate the correct techniques for laying and securing cables in various environments (e.g., ceilings, walls, and floors).
Identify appropriate cable types and routing methods for different applications and environments.
Implement cable management practices, such as using cable ties, raceways, and conduits to organize and protect cables.
Ensure compliance with industry standards and regulations for cable routing and installation.

learning_outcomes.description: Install connectors and terminations accurately

performance_criteria.description: Identify and select the appropriate connectors for different types of cables (e.g., RJ45 for twisted pair, LC/SC for fiber optic).
Demonstrate the correct procedure for terminating cables with connectors, including stripping, crimping, and securing.
Verify that terminations are done correctly by testing and inspecting connectors for proper alignment and secure connections.
Troubleshoot and resolve issues with connector terminations, such as poor connections or signal loss
Document the types and locations of connectors used in the installation for future reference and maintenance.

learning_outcomes.description: Install and configure network components

performance_criteria.description: Describe the installation process for network components such as patch panels, wall plates, and network jacks
Demonstrate how to mount and secure network components in racks, cabinets, or on walls according to industry best practices.
Connect and configure network components to ensure they function correctly with the installed cabling.
Perform cable testing and verification after installation to confirm that all components are properly connected and operational.
Ensure that installed network components are organized and labeled for easy identification and troubleshooting.

learning_outcomes.description: Conduct post-installation checks and adjustments

performance_criteria.description: Perform a visual inspection of the installed cabling to ensure it meets installation standards and is free from damage.
Test network connections using appropriate testing equipment to verify signal strength, continuity, and performance.
Make any necessary adjustments to cables, connectors, or network components to correct issues identified during testing.
Document and report any issues or discrepancies discovered during post-installation checks and the steps taken to resolve them.

learning_outcomes.description: Understand the importance and objectives of cabling testing and certification

performance_criteria.description: Explain the purpose of cabling testing and certification in ensuring network reliability and performance.
Describe the key performance parameters for network cabling, such as signal integrity, attenuation, and crosstalk.
Identify industry standards and certification requirements for network cabling (e.g., TIA/EIA, ISO/IEC).
Discuss the implications of failing to properly test and certify network cabling.

learning_outcomes.description: Conduct comprehensive cabling tests

performance_criteria.description: Execute tests for continuity, signal strength, and performance using appropriate testing equipment.
Perform advanced tests for parameters such as impedance, attenuation, and near-end crosstalk (NEXT).
Interpret test results to identify issues such as cable faults, performance degradation, or improper terminations.
Document and report test results clearly, including any anomalies or issues detected.

learning_outcomes.description: Troubleshoot and resolve cabling issues

performance_criteria.description: Analyse test results to diagnose common cabling issues, such as signal loss, short circuits, or interference.
Implement troubleshooting techniques to isolate and fix identified issues in the cabling system.
Re-test cables and connections after troubleshooting to ensure that issues have been resolved and performance meets standards.
Document the troubleshooting process and resolution steps for future reference.

learning_outcomes.description: Prepare and maintain certification documentation

performance_criteria.description: Compile and organize test results and certification reports according to industry standards and client requirements.
Ensure that all documentation is accurate, complete, and clearly formatted.
Maintain records of all testing and certification activities for future reference and compliance audits.
Explain the process for submitting certification reports to clients or regulatory bodies, including any required approvals or signatures.

learning_outcomes.description: Identify and diagnose common network cabling issues

performance_criteria.description: Describe typical problems in network cabling systems, such as signal loss, intermittent connectivity, and physical damage.
Use diagnostic tools and techniques to identify the root causes of network issues, including continuity testers and network analyzers.
Analyze symptoms and test results to pinpoint specific cabling problems, such as shorts, opens, or miswiring.
Document observed issues and their potential causes to aid in troubleshooting and resolution.

learning_outcomes.description: Perform basic repairs and maintenance on network cabling

performance_criteria.description: Demonstrate the ability to perform repairs on faulty cables, including splicing or replacing damaged sections.
Re-terminate connectors and reconfigure terminations as needed to resolve issues with connectivity or performance.
Conduct routine maintenance tasks, such as checking cable integrity, cleaning connectors, and verifying cable management.
Test repaired or maintained cables to ensure they meet performance standards and function correctly.

learning_outcomes.description: Implement preventive maintenance strategies

performance_criteria.description: Develop and follow a preventive maintenance schedule to regularly inspect and service network cabling systems.
Identify and address potential issues before they cause significant problems, such as monitoring for signs of wear and tear or environmental factors affecting cabling.
Apply best practices for cable management and organization to prevent future issues and ensure system longevity.
Educate team members or users about proper cable handling and maintenance practices to reduce the likelihood of damage.

learning_outcomes.description: Use diagnostic tools effectively for troubleshooting

performance_criteria.description: Identify and operate various diagnostic tools, such as cable testers, network analysers, and optical time-domain reflectometers (OTDR).
Interpret the output of diagnostic tools to determine the nature and location of network issues.
Perform tests and measurements, such as cable length, signal attenuation, and bit error rate, to assess network performance.
Record results to guide troubleshooting efforts and verify that issues have been resolved.

learning_outcomes.description: Document troubleshooting and maintenance activities

performance_criteria.description: Create detailed records of troubleshooting steps, repairs performed, and maintenance activities conducted.
Document any changes made to the network cabling system, including modifications to configurations or installations.
Maintain logs of recurring issues and resolutions to help identify patterns and inform future maintenance strategies.
Prepare and present reports on troubleshooting and maintenance activities for review by supervisors or clients.

learning_outcomes.description: Follow safety procedures during troubleshooting and maintenance

performance_criteria.description: Adhere to safety protocols when working with network cabling systems, including using appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE).
Follow safe practices when handling tools and equipment to prevent accidents and injuries.
Ensure that the work area is safe and free from hazards during troubleshooting and maintenance activities.
Respond appropriately to emergencies or accidents, including reporting incidents and taking corrective actions as needed.

units.title: Introduction to Industry Standards and Best Practices

learning_outcomes.description: Understand key industry standards for network cabling

performance_criteria.description: Identify and describe the key industry standards related to network cabling, including TIA/EIA, ISO/IEC, and IEEE standards.
Explain the purpose of these standards and how they contribute to the quality, safety, and performance of network cabling systems.
Discuss the process of updating and revising standards and the impact of these changes on network installations.
Explain how compliance with these standards is verified and documented during network installations and inspections.

learning_outcomes.description: Apply best practices for network cabling installation

performance_criteria.description: Describe best practices for cable routing, including minimizing bends, avoiding interference, and maintaining separation from electrical cables.
Demonstrate proper techniques for cable preparation and termination, ensuring adherence to standards for performance and reliability.
Implement best practices for cable management, including the use of cable trays, ties, and labels to organize and protect cables.
Follow recommended installation procedures for network components such as patch panels, jacks, and racks to ensure optimal performance and ease of maintenance.

learning_outcomes.description: Ensure compliance with safety and environmental regulations

performance_criteria.description: Identify relevant safety regulations and guidelines for network cabling work, including those related to electrical safety and fire protection.
Apply environmental best practices, such as proper disposal of waste materials and minimizing environmental impact during installations.
Demonstrate knowledge of and compliance with workplace health and safety requirements, including the use of personal protective equipment (PPE) and safe work practices.
Explain how to conduct risk assessments and implement safety measures to address potential hazards in network cabling environments.

learning_outcomes.description: Utilize documentation and reporting standards

performance_criteria.description: Create and maintain detailed documentation of network cabling installations, including design schematics, installation procedures, and component specifications.
Follow reporting standards for documenting compliance with industry standards and regulations, including test results and certification reports.
Ensure that all documentation is accurate, up-to-date, and accessible for future reference and audits.
Prepare clear and professional reports on network cabling projects, including summaries of compliance with standards and any deviations or issues encountered.

learning_outcomes.description: Review and implement industry best practices for network maintenance

performance_criteria.description: Identify best practices for ongoing maintenance of network cabling systems, including regular inspections, testing, and troubleshooting procedures.
Apply best practices for updating and upgrading network infrastructure to accommodate new technologies or changing requirements.
Implement procedures for ensuring network cabling systems remain compliant with evolving industry standards and best practices.
Educate team members or clients on the importance of adhering to best practices and industry standards in maintaining network cabling systems.

units.title: Use of Tools and Equipment in Network Cabling

learning_outcomes.description: Identify and describe common tools and equipment used in network cabling

performance_criteria.description: List and describe the functions of essential network cabling tools, including cable testers, crimpers, punch-down tools, and cable strippers.
Explain the purpose and use of specialized equipment such as optical time-domain reflectometers (OTDR), network analyzers, and cable certifiers.
Identify various hand tools and power tools used in cabling installations, such as drills, wire cutters, and scissors.
Describe the features and benefits of each tool or piece of equipment in relation to its application in network cabling.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate correct usage of tools and equipment

performance_criteria.description: Show proper handling techniques for tools to prevent damage to cables and ensure safety during use.
Demonstrate the correct procedures for using cable testers and certifiers to evaluate cable performance and identify faults.
Use crimpers and punch-down tools accurately to terminate cables and secure connections, ensuring proper alignment and functionality.
Perform cable stripping and preparation using appropriate tools, maintaining cable integrity and preparing for termination or connection.

learning_outcomes.description: Perform maintenance and calibration of tools and equipment

performance_criteria.description: Conduct regular maintenance on network cabling tools, including cleaning, lubricating, and inspecting for wear and tear.
Calibrate testing equipment as needed to ensure accuracy and reliability in measurements and results.
Identify and address common issues with tools and equipment, such as misalignment, malfunction, or damage.
Replace or repair tools and equipment as necessary to maintain optimal performance and safety standards.

learning_outcomes.description: Ensure safety and compliance during tool and equipment use

performance_criteria.description: Follow safety protocols for using tools and equipment, including wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) and adhering to safety guidelines.
Demonstrate knowledge of safety practices related to electrical hazards, tool handling, and working in confined or elevated spaces.
Store tools and equipment properly when not in use to prevent accidents and damage.
Report and document any safety incidents or equipment malfunctions, following appropriate procedures for incident management and resolution.
